findings.description: In "He had at that time² no notion of¹", "had" is the first piece of phrase 1 (have no notion of) and "at that time" is phrase 2. Both are red with no space or mark between them, so the screen shows "had at that time²" as one phrase numbered 2 and "no notion of¹" as a separate phrase. A viewer would link "had" to entry 2 (at that time) instead of entry 1 (have no notion of), and the badges read 2, 1, 3 from left to right. Checked at 2x zoom: the two pieces are drawn as one continuous red run.

In "had been borrowed for the day⁵ from⁴ Mr. Albert Griggs⁶", "borrowed" is the first piece of phrase 4 (borrow…from) and "for the day" is phrase 5. Both are red and run together, so the screen shows "borrowed for the day⁵" as one phrase numbered 5 and a lone "from⁴". A viewer cannot tell that "borrowed" belongs to entry 4 (borrow…from) rather than entry 5 (for the day). Confirmed at 2x zoom: there is no separation between the two pieces.

The vocabulary panel (16 entries) is packed to its edges. The red VOCABULARY label starts about 5 px below the panel's top outline (y≈145, outline at y=140). The descender of "p" in the last entry "stupid" reaches y=982 and touches the bottom outline at y=983. Most screens have about 20 px or more of padding, and even screens 15, 23 and 52 keep about 15 px. Nothing is cut off yet, but the text touches the frame and has no margin.

The highlighted words match the reference, but the way they are drawn is misleading. The phrase 'have no notion of' (entry 1, highlighted words 'had … no notion of') has its unnumbered first piece 'had' sitting directly next to entry 2 'at that time'. Both are the same red bold with no gap between them, so the line reads as one run, 'had at that time[2] no notion of[1]'. A viewer would take entry 2 to be 'had at that time' and would not link 'had' to entry 1. Nothing on screen marks 'had' as belonging to entry 1.

Same problem as screen 8. The highlighted words match the reference ('borrowed … from' for entry 4 and 'for the day' for entry 5), but the unnumbered piece 'borrowed' of 'borrow…from' (entry 4) runs straight into 'for the day' (entry 5) in the same red bold. The screen therefore reads 'borrowed for the day[5] from[4]', so 'borrowed' looks like part of entry 5 rather than entry 4.
